$comment: TU Berlin — the ninth AOI, and the FIRST one outside UTM zone 32. Everything Berlin surveys is published in EPSG:25833, and that is not a question of precision but of whether a download exists at all: the DGM1 and LoD2 tile FILENAMES encode zone-33 kilometres, so this campus is `DGM1_386_5818` in zone 33 and `DGM1_793_5827` — a file that does not exist — in zone 32. Adding this site is what made `tools/geodata/utm.py` take the zone from the AOI instead of hard-coding it, and what made `load_aoi` bind that zone so no pipeline step can forget it. Berlin is also the fifth geobasis authority here, after the LDBV (Bayern), the LGL (Baden-Württemberg), Geobasis NRW and the LGV (Hamburg).

campuses.anchorSource: OSM relation/2138962 name='Technische Universität Berlin' — the main campus polygon between Ernst-Reuter-Platz, Straße des 17. Juni and the Landwehrkanal
campuses.$bboxComment: ~1609 x 2405 m. MEASURED extent of the 196 strictly-TU-Berlin OSM features clustered here (2026-08-26): west 13.31987, east 13.33542, south 52.50750, north 52.52431, plus the ~250 m margin the other AOIs carry. The box deliberately reaches north to the Sportzentrum Dovestraße and the Severin-Gelände, which are TU Berlin and would otherwise sit on the edge.

campuses.anchorSource: OSM way/26410648 name='TIB 15', Gustav-Meyer-Allee — the Technologie- und Innovationspark Berlin, where TU Berlin's Institut für Bauingenieurwesen, Fachgebiet Kraftfahrzeuge and Forschungszentrum Strangpressen sit
campuses.$bboxComment: ~712 x 939 m. MEASURED extent of the 14 strictly-TU-Berlin features clustered here: west 13.38345, east 13.38631, south 52.53858, north 52.54235, plus 250 m. ⚠️ CORRECTION TO AN ASSUMPTION: the second campus was planned as 'Wedding (Seestraße)'. The probe found that Seestraße holds exactly ONE TU Berlin feature — way/705175020, the Gebäudekomplex Gärungsgewerbe-Biotechnologie — while the substantial second site is the TIB at Gustav-Meyer-Allee, 1.5 km further east. A single building is not a campus, so the AOI is built around the site that is one.

campusSeparation.$comment: MEASURED between the two anchors above, projected into EPSG:25833: 4999 m. Haversine cross-check on the same pair: 4989 m. ⚠️ THIS IS THE LARGEST SEPARATION IN THE PORTFOLIO by a wide margin — FAU Erlangen's 2.88 km was the previous record, and OTH's 2.48 km is the one the shuttle narrative was originally built around. It is also what forces the 5.11 x 4.49 km core box below, and with it the 1.25 m/px drape: at the 4096 px cap those two numbers are the same decision seen from two sides.

ownership.$comment: How a TU Berlin building is recognised. ⚠️ THE OBVIOUS PATTERN IS THE DANGEROUS ONE HERE. An Overpass sweep of the wide box returned Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin (relation/2138961, /6670113, /12741778), the Universität der Künste (relation/14720811), the HWR (relation/8422596) and the BHT — all `amenity=university`, all in the same city, several within walking distance of the Straße des 17. Juni. 'Universität Berlin' as a substring matches the Freie Universität and the Humboldt-Universität as well; only the full 'Technische Universität Berlin' identifies this one, exactly as Köln needs its full form to exclude TH Köln.
ownership.$outlineComment: relation/2138962 is the Charlottenburg campus polygon. relation/1273140 is the university-wide relation, whose centroid (52.48873) lands outside BOTH campuses because it spans sites across the city — so it is useful as an ownership test and useless as an anchor, which is why the anchors above come from the campus polygon and a named building instead.
ownership.$extraComment: The TIB buildings, claimed by hand. ⚠️ TIB 16, TIB17 and TIB17a are tagged `building=industrial` and operated by the technology park rather than by the university — TU Berlin is one tenant among several, the same tenancy situation TechBase creates at OTH. What justifies the entries is TU Berlin's own statement of presence: OSM node/4007032904 'TU Berlin Institut für Bauingenieurwesen', node/4007032901 'TU Berlin Fachgebiet Kraftfahrzeuge' and node/13928987501 'Forschungszentrum Strangpressen der TU Berlin' all sit inside these footprints. An allow-list is the right instrument precisely because a rule general enough to catch them would also catch the neighbours.

bbox.$comment: PHOTOREAL CORE, 5.11 x 4.49 km in EPSG:25833 (E 385716..390823, N 5818460..5822945), covering BOTH campuses AND the corridor between them. The corridor is not padding: the whole point of the twin is to make the inter-campus transition visible, so the ground between the two sites has to be rendered rather than implied. 2553 x 2243 samples at the 2 m grid below = 11.5 MB uint16, comfortably inside the 32 MB budget the config test enforces.

shell.$comment: COARSE TERRAIN SHELL, ~27.8 x 24.5 km. ⚠️ AND IT HAS ALMOST NOTHING TO SHOW, which is worth saying plainly rather than discovering in the render. Regensburg's shell carries the Danube valley and the Bayerischer-Wald foothills; Berlin's carries the Teltow and Barnim plateaux either side of the Urstromtal, which is tens of metres of relief across tens of kilometres. The shell here is doing the job it does at Garching — closing the horizon so the core does not end in mid-air — not providing scenery. Fits entirely inside the single Copernicus tile N52_E013.

$workingCrsComment: ⚠️ THE ONLY NON-25832 AOI IN THIS REPOSITORY, and the reason `load_aoi` cross-checks this field against the box's own geometry. Berlin publishes DGM1, DOP20 and LoD2 exclusively in EPSG:25833. Left on EPSG:25832 by a copy-paste, this AOI would not merely be imprecise — the terrain and building fetchers build their download URLs from zone kilometres and would ask for tiles that do not exist, while the drape WMS would happily return a photograph of somewhere near Kassel.

elevationRangeM.$comment: MEASURED 2026-08-26 by build_terrain.py over the core: 15.99 .. 69.46 m, from 12 Berlin DGM1 tiles at 100% coverage. The declared bracket is left deliberately loose around the measurement so a re-run after a data update does not trip the plausibility gate over a decimetre. ⚠️ THE 16 m MINIMUM WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ACCEPTED, because a first draft declared 25 m and the gate rejected the build. It is 304 cells — 0.12 ha — in one patch at 52.5358/13.3742, the Berlin-Spandauer Schifffahrtskanal basin at Nordhafen, i.e. a lock or dock structure the bare-earth model reads down into. Only 3.3 ha of the whole 22 km² core lies below 30 m. The maximum lands at 52.5442/13.3872, which is the Gustav-Meyer-Höhe in Volkspark Humboldthain and agrees with that summit's published 68 m to 0.32 m. CONSEQUENCE: this is the FLATTEST site in the portfolio — about 35 m of relief across 5 km against OTH's 78 m across 3 km — so essentially none of the realism here comes from the landform. It has to come from the 20 cm orthophoto, the LoD2 roofs and the trees, and per the standing rule the terrain is NOT to be vertically exaggerated to compensate.

verification.$comment: Registration gate. ⚠️ THE CONTROL POINTS WERE TRIAGED, NOT COLLECTED. An Overpass sweep found 35 `ele`-tagged nodes inside the core, and most are unusable: six `man_made=surveillance` cameras all carry ele=39.0 (one nearby reads 2.5 m, which gives the game away — these are MOUNTING heights, not ground elevations), and the cluster of bare `ele` nodes along the Ringbahn between 13.383 and 13.389 are railway survey heights on embankments and bridges. What is left, and what is listed below, are the `natural`-tagged ground features. The 'GPS-Referenzpunkt BerlinMitte' (node/1786272742, ele=79.8, ele:nhn) was deliberately EXCLUDED for the same reason as the cameras: it is a reference mark whose published height need not be the ground under it.

controlPoints.name: Gustav-Meyer-Höhe
controlPoints.source: OSM node/11831664671 natural + name + source, Volkspark Humboldthain

controlPoints.name: Großer Bunkerberg
controlPoints.source: OSM node/1586382882 natural=peak + wikidata, Volkspark Friedrichshain, ele=78

controlPoints.name: Fichtenberg
controlPoints.source: OSM node/354006455 natural=peak + wikidata + wikipedia, ele=68

verification.$controlPointsComment: THREE in the core and five in the shell. ⚠️ A FOURTH CORE POINT WAS REMOVED AFTER IT FAILED, and the reason it failed is the reason it should never have been trusted: OSM node/1333652275 carries natural=peak and ele=46 at 52.5115/13.3393, but its only documentation is `wikipedia=de:Berliner Flaktürme` and `wikimedia_commons=Category:Flak towers in Berlin` — a Berlin-wide article about DEMOLISHED structures, not a survey of this mound. The model reads 42.88 m against that quoted 46, a 3.12 m miss on a 3.0 m tolerance. A round number sourced to a general article is a quotation, not a measurement, and the three core points that remain all agree to better than 1.5 m. ⚠️ ARKENBERGE WAS ALSO REMOVED, AND THAT ONE IS NOT A DATA-QUALITY PROBLEM AT ALL. At 121.9 m it is the highest point in Berlin and properly documented, but it is a LANDFILL THAT IS STILL BEING RAISED: the Copernicus GLO-30 radar (TanDEM-X, acquired 2010–2015) measured it at 105.9 m and it has grown some 16 m since. The gate reported -15.96 m against a 12 m tolerance and was right to — a control point has to be a fixed thing, and this one is a construction site. ⚠️ NEARLY EVERY REMAINING POINT IS A TRÜMMERBERG: Teufelsberg, Drachenberg, the Bunkerberge, the Insulaner and the Gustav-Meyer-Höhe are all war rubble. That is not a caveat about their accuracy, they are properly surveyed; it is why a city on an outwash plain has any relief to register against at all. The two wooded ones (Großer Bunkerberg +6.99 m, Fichtenberg +6.38 m) sit high because the shell is a SURFACE model and reads their canopy, exactly as the seam-offset note describes.

drape.$comment: Long side of the DOP20 mosaic. At the 5.11 km core this is 1.25 m per pixel — the COARSEST drape in the portfolio (Garching 0.61, Tübingen 0.63, OTH 0.78, LMU 0.96), and a direct consequence of holding two campuses 5 km apart in one box. It is still far finer than the 2 m terrain grid beneath it. NOT larger: at 8192 px the mipmap chain is ~300 MB, which Chromium accepts and then silently samples BLACK. This box is not square, so 4096 x 3598 px lands near 78 MB — about where OTH sits, i.e. the size known to upload reliably.

grids.$comment: Berlin ATKIS DGM1 (1 m XYZ) resampled to a 2 m heightmap, mesh decimated 2x -> 4 m posting. The core is the largest in the repository, so this is also the largest vertex budget; the site being almost flat is what makes that affordable, since a decimated mesh loses nothing where there is no relief to lose.

shellGrids.$comment: Copernicus GLO-30 -> ~90 m posting. transitionBandM is expressed in metres for readability but MUST be applied as a fraction of the core (CORE_FADE_FRACTION ~0.08), never absolute.

$focusPlacesComment: All twelve resolved from the OSM probe of 2026-08-26 — no coordinate here was typed from memory or from a map read by eye. Ten sit on the Charlottenburg campus and two at the TIB, which is the honest ratio: 196 of the 228 strictly-TU-Berlin features in the wide box are in Charlottenburg.
$lensesComment: The OTH/LMU set exactly. ⚠️ `flow` IS ABSENT AND CANNOT BE ADDED HERE. Flow is routed from REAL consecutive course bookings, which only Garching has (TUMonline via NavigaTUM). Inventing where people walk across a campus is a materially bigger claim than inventing a utilisation percentage and would look just as authoritative on screen, so the lens is withheld rather than filled with a guess. ⚠️ `condition` IS ALSO ABSENT, DELIBERATELY. It was in the first draft of this config on the reasoning that more lenses is more parity; it is not — Tübingen is the ONLY site in this repository that carries it, and its scores, grades and renovation costs are entirely invented. Putting a fabricated backlog of deferred maintenance on a named university's real buildings is a different kind of claim from a fabricated timetable, and it is not one this AOI needs to make.

planQuality.source: tools/data/build_plan_quality.py — whole-cohort lecture days + slot desirability

indoorProbe.$comment: ⚠️ 235 `indoor=room` FEATURES IN THE CHARLOTTENBURG BOX, AND ESSENTIALLY NONE OF THEM ARE TU BERLIN'S. The probe of 2026-08-26 returned 1 726 indoor/level features and 235 rooms; reading their names shows what they actually are — 'DB Reisezentrum', 'BVG', 'Ditsch', 'M-Markt', 'China Box', 'Bistro Avci', 'Skyline' — the retail units inside Bahnhof Zoologischer Garten, which sits just outside the campus and well inside the box. NOT ONE of the 235 carries a `ref` tag. This is exactly the trap the OTH entry warns about in the other direction: a healthy-looking count that means nothing once you ask whose rooms they are.
indoorProbe.$conclusion: No usable surveyed interiors. TU Berlin publishes no open floor plans and there is no NavigaTUM equivalent, so every room is generated inside the real footprint at the real storey count and badged as such — the RWTH Aachen situation, not the OTH or LMU one.

rooms.$comment: ⚠️ EVERY ROOM INTERIOR ON THIS SITE IS GENERATED — plates laid out inside the REAL footprint at the REAL storey count, badged `generated` on every record. What IS real here is the building and its identifier: TU Berlin publishes its building letters and OpenStreetMap carries 30 of them as feature names (A, AM, B, BA, BH-A, BH-N, E, E-N, ER, EW, F, HF, HL, K, KF, KT, KWT, L, M, MAR, MS, SE, TAP, TC, TEM, TK, V, W, Z and the named Hauptgebäude, Mathematikgebäude, Erweiterungsbau, Chemiegebäude), each with a street address. Occupancy comes from the generated timetable rather than being invented separately, so the colour a room takes IS the plan the solver is working on.
rooms.$codePatternComment: ⚠️ UPPER CASE, AND THE CASE IS DELIBERATE — the opposite call from RWTH Aachen. There a lower-case building letter is the provenance signal, because RWTH publishes no letters and the identifiers are ours. TU Berlin DOES publish its letters and OSM has surveyed them, so writing them lower case would disown a real identifier. The room NUMBER after the letter is still generated; the letter is not. The pattern allows the hyphenated forms OSM actually carries (BH-A, BH-N, A-F, E-N) and both 3- and 4-digit room numbers, since TU Berlin uses 'MA 041' and 'H 1012' alike.
rooms.$heroBuildingComment: The Hauptgebäude on Straße des 17. Juni (OSM relation/3348239). Chosen because it is the building a visitor to TU Berlin actually pictures, it carries the big lecture halls, and it sits at the centre of the Charlottenburg cluster — so the demo opens on the densest, most recognisable part of the twin rather than on a shed.

geobasis.attribution: Datenquelle: Geoportal Berlin, Land Berlin, dl-de/zero-2-0
geobasis.$comment: ⚠️ dl-de/zero-2-0 REQUIRES NO ATTRIBUTION AT ALL — the most permissive of the five authorities in this pipeline, against CC BY 4.0 in Bayern and dl-de/by-2-0 in Baden-Württemberg, NRW and Hamburg. It is given anyway, because this app tells the user where every layer it draws came from, and 'we were not obliged to say' is a poor answer to 'whose photograph is this'. ⚠️ THE CATALOGUE LIVES AT datenregister.berlin.de, NOT daten.berlin.de — the latter's /api/3/action/ path 404s, which is the kind of dead end that reads as 'Berlin has no open data API'.

products.dgm1: ATOM, DGM1_<E>_<N>.zip on a 2 km EVEN-parity grid; the member is ASCII XYZ (dgm1_33_<E>_<N>_2_be.xyz) despite the catalogue calling it CSV
products.lod2: ATOM, LoD2_<E>_<N>.zip on a 1 km grid; the member is CityGML with an .xml suffix, rewritten to .gml on extraction because build_lod2_mesh.py globs for *.gml
products.dop20: WMS only — layer `dop_2025` on services/wms/dop_2025_fruehjahr. ⚠️ NEVER the ATOM download: it is partitioned by district and Mitte.zip alone is 3.2 GB.

shellGeobasis.attribution: produced using Copernicus WorldDEM-30 © DLR e.V. 2010–2014 and © Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014–2018 provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA; all rights reserved
shellGeobasis.$attributionComment: The ADAPTED-DATA form of the notice, which is prescribed rather than stylistic: the pipeline resamples the tile onto a UTM grid and shifts it onto the core's vertical datum, so it is unambiguously modified.
shellGeobasis.$tilesComment: ONE tile, unlike OTH's four: the shell spans 52.42–52.64 N and 13.15–13.56 E, crossing neither the 53 N parallel nor the 14 E meridian.

$tourComment: Four stops, ending at the TIB so the 5 km transfer is something the viewer watches happen rather than reads about. The opening range is 1400 m against OTH's 1200 because the core here is nearly twice as wide.
